zoroastrianismzoroastrianismn.def: The religious system of Zoroaster, the legislator and prophet of the ancient Persians, which was the national faith of Persia; mazdeism.

zosterazosteranetym.def: A genus of plants of the Naiadaceæ, or Pondweed family.

zosteropszosteropsnetym.def: A genus of birds that comprises the white-eyes.

zoundszoundsinterjetym.def: An exclamation formerly used as an oath, and an expression of anger or wonder.

zoutchzoutchvt.def: To stew, as flounders, eels, etc., with just enough or liquid to cover them.

zuchettozuchettonetym.def: A skullcap covering the tonsure, worn under the berretta.

zufolozufolonetym.def: A little flute or flageolet, especially that which is used to teach birds.

zulukaffirzulukaffirn.def: A member of the Bantu race comprising the Zulus and the Kaffirs.

zuluszulusnpl.def: The most important tribe belonging to the Kaffir race.

zumboorukzumbooruknetym.def: A small cannon supported by a swiveled rest on the back of a camel, whence it is fired, — used in the East.

zuniszunisnpl.def: A tribe of Pueblo Indians occupying a village in New Mexico, on the Zuni River.

zunyitezunyiten.def: A fluosilicate of alumina occurring in tetrahedral crystals at the Zuñi mine in Colorado.

zwanzigerzwanzigernetym.def: Am Austrian silver coin equivalent to 20 kreutzers, or about 10 cents.

zwiebackzwiebackn.def: A kind of biscuit or rusk first baked in a loaf and afterwards cut and toasted.

zwinglianzwingliana.def: Of or pertaining to Ulric Zwingli (1481-1531), the reformer of German Switzerland, who maintained that in the Lord's Supper the true body of Christ is present by the contemplation of faith but not in essence or reality, and that the sacrament is a memorial without mystical elements.

zygapophysiszygapophysisn.def: One of the articular processes of a vertebra, of which there are usually four, two anterior and two posterior.

zygenidzygenidnetym.def: Any one of numerous species of moths of the family Zygænidæ, most of which are bright colored.

zygobranchiazygobranchianpl.def: A division of marine gastropods in which the gills are developed on both sides of the body and the renal organs are also paired.

zygobranchiatezygobranchiatea.def: Of or pertaining to the Zygobranchia.

zygodactylic.def: Yoke-footed; having the toes disposed in pairs; — applied to birds which have two toes before and two behind, as the parrot, cuckoo, woodpecker, etc.

zygomaticzygomaticaetym.def: Of, pertaining to, or in the region of, the zygoma.

zygomorphic.def: Symmetrical bilaterally; — said of organisms, or parts of organisms, capable of division into two symmetrical halves only in a single plane.

zygophytezygophytenetym.def: Any plant of a proposed class or grand division (Zygophytes, Zygophyta, or Zygosporeæ), in which reproduction consists in the union of two similar cells.

zygospermzygospermnetym.def: A spore formed by the union of the contents of two similar cells, either of the same or of distinct individual plants.

zygosphenezygosphenenetym.def: A median process on the front part of the neural arch of the vertebræ of most snakes and some lizards, which fits into a fossa, called the zygantrum, on the back part of the arch in front.

aferment.def: The morbific principle of a zymotic disease.

zymiczymica.def: Pertaining to, or produced by, fermentation; — formerly, by confusion, used to designate lactic acid.

zymogenzymogennetym.def: A mother substance, or antecedent, of an enzyme or chemical ferment; — applied to such substances as, not being themselves actual ferments, may by internal changes give rise to a ferment.

zymogenezymogenenetym.def: One of a physiological group of globular bacteria which produces fermentations of diverse nature; — distinguished from pathogene.

zymologistzymologistn.def: One who is skilled in zymology, or in the fermentation of liquors.

zymologyzymologynetym.def: A treatise on the fermentation of liquors, or the doctrine of fermentation.

zymolysiszymolysisn.def: The action of enzymes; also, the changes produced by such action.

zymomezymomenetym.def: A glutinous substance, insoluble in alcohol, resembling legumin; — now called vegetable fibrin, vegetable albumin, or gluten casein.

zymometer.def: An instrument for ascertaining the degree of fermentation occasioned by the mixture of different liquids, and the degree of heat which they acquire in fermentation.

zythumzythumnetym.def: A kind of ancient malt beverage; a liquor made from malt and wheat.
